trust_decision.summary: Which PAX records of an entry are honoured: the header/size parser in poll_next_raw rejects malformed records with an error, while the path, linkpath and xattr readers in entry.rs silently drop malformed records and keep scanning, so the two readers of one PAX block can disagree.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'insufficiently validates PAX extensions during extraction'; EntryFields::path_bytes is where the PAX 'path' key decides the extraction path, and its filter_map(|f| f.ok()) is the obvious place to look.

fix_sites.entry_point: Entry::path / Entry::path_bytes (public API) and Archive::unpack / Entry::unpack_in / Entry::unpack_in_raw via EntryFields::unpack_in at src/entry.rs:496
Entry::link_name / Entry::link_name_bytes (public API) and Entry::unpack for symlink/hardlink at src/entry.rs:601

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: src/entry.rs:907-918 (set_xattrs, reached only with the xattr feature and unpack_xattrs enabled); also src/archive.rs:296 directory sort in Archive::unpack

O3_reason_to_dismiss: set_xattrs is an opt-in, unix-only metadata feature unrelated to path selection, so a solver focused on the 'path' key can argue malformed xattr records are harmless to skip.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Well-formed PAX records with non-UTF-8 keys must still be skipped (not rejected) by the size/uid/gid pass, and PAX 'path' must keep precedence over the ustar header while a GNU long name still overrides PAX; an over-broad fix that rejects any unknown/non-UTF-8 key or reorders precedence breaks pax_precedence/pax_path tests.

O6_input_shapes: malformed record (length prefix mismatch) before the 'path' key

O8_uncovered_routes.route: PAX record framing splits on '\n' instead of honouring the decimal length prefix, so a value containing a newline is parsed differently from POSIX-conforming tar tools; unchanged by the fix.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The parser is shared by every reader inside the crate, so it is internally consistent; the mismatch is only with other tar implementations.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: separate file (src/pax.rs) from the landing point

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Duplicate PAX keys: size/uid/gid take the last occurrence (loop overwrites) while path/linkpath take the first occurrence (early return), and the fix keeps first-wins for path.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Duplicate keys are not 'malformed' records, so a solver can say they fall outside a malformed-extension advisory.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: The PAX buffer that poll_next_raw uses for size override (self.current.4) is set when a local PAX header is read and never cleared, while the per-entry copy used for path is take()n; later entries may get an earlier entry's PAX size but not its path.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Looks like state plumbing from an earlier fix rather than validation; the advisory talks about malformed records, not stale ones.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: src/archive.rs, Entries::poll_next state, not on the path from the report

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a planted 'mtime'/'mode' PAX override in poll_next_raw that skips malformed records with filter_map like the path reader
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The size/uid/gid override loop is the natural place a maintainer would extend PAX support, and copying the entry.rs idiom would be easy.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Entry::pax_extensions consumers (e.g. a helper resolving 'linkpath' for hard links) that drop errors
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Public iterator returns io::Result items; callers ignoring errors is the idiom already used in three places.

O9_family: parser differential / interpretation conflict (CWE-436) on tar PAX extended headers

O10_build.project_tests: tests/all.rs (pax_simple, pax_pending_interrupted, pax_path, pax_precedence at tests/all.rs:888-994) and tests/entry.rs; xattr tests need a unix filesystem with user xattrs

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Replace filter_map(|f| f.ok()) with error propagation in path_bytes only, leaving link_name_bytes and set_xattrs silently skipping malformed records.

out_of_scope_notes: Global PAX headers ('g') are not applied to size or path in Entries (only local 'x' handled at src/archive.rs:433); not pursued.
